metaDescription: Five cordless hedge trimmers under $200 with brushless motors, 24-inch blades and two-battery kits, compared on real cutting capacity and ownership.
expertTake: The 24-inch brushless two-battery trimmer is the best overall for blade length and runtime. The Greenworks 24V brushless is the pick for cleanest cuts on thick stems. Anyone with hedges thicker than an inch of woody growth should skip trimmers and buy a pole saw or loppers.
introParagraphs: The upper end of the hedge trimmer market is where battery runtime and motor design start to matter more than blade length. A longer job needs a second battery, and a harder-working motor needs to be brushless. Pick the trimmer by hedge length and wood type first, then by battery.

The cap here is $200, and prices move, so it reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. This tier is for owners with long hedges and for anyone who has outgrown a basic trimmer after a season of use. Long hedges reward spare batteries, and stiff stems reward fast strokes.

products.name: 24-Inch Brushless Cordless Hedge Trimmer, 2 Batteries, 3000RPM
products.description:
This trimmer pairs a brushless motor with a 24-inch dual-action steel blade and ships with two rechargeable batteries and a charger. The listing quotes a 1200-watt rating and 3,000 RPM. A watt figure on a battery tool is a peak input number, so treat it as a ceiling rather than continuous output, but the brushless design backs it up with real efficiency gains.

A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat and has no brushes to wear, which is why it earns the top spot for a tool that may run for an hour on a big hedge. Two batteries mean you can swap mid-job and charge the spare. The 24-inch blade is the longest class and covers a long hedge in fewer passes, at the price of tip weight.

Compared with the Greenworks 24V it has four inches more blade, a second battery and no stated debris collector. It is a lesser-known brand, so check the warranty, spare battery availability and the capacity stated in the manual. Wipe and oil the blade after each use and store the batteries indoors. In year three, the batteries will be the first thing to fade, so buy a spare while the kit is still listed. Keep the vents clear and the blade bolts snug.
products.bestFor: Long hedges where a brushless motor and spare battery both matter.
pros: Brushless motor runs cooler and wears less
24 inch blade covers long hedges quickly
cons: Tip weight tires arms on long sessions

products.name: Greenworks 24V 20-Inch Brushless Hedge Trimmer, 1.1-Inch Capacity
products.description:
The Greenworks 24V is the quality pick: a 20-inch dual-action blade running at 4,000 strokes per minute with a stated capacity of 1.1 inches, driven by a brushless motor. High stroke rate matters because it slices stems cleanly instead of tearing them, which leaves tips that heal brown-free.

It includes a 2.0Ah battery and charger and a debris collector that sweeps clippings aside, which cuts raking time afterward. A wrap-around handle gives multiple cutting positions.

Against the 24-inch brushless it has less blade and one battery, but its stroke rate and capacity are higher. It is the better pick if your hedge has stiff stems and your sessions are short. Oil the blade and keep the battery indoors. Compared with the 22-inch Ryobi, the extra stroke speed shows most on hedges with hard, woody stems. A single battery means planning breaks around the charger, so charge it before you start. The debris collector is a small feature that saves a surprising amount of raking when you trim a hedge over a path or patio.
products.bestFor: Stiff stems and clean cut tips on short to medium sessions.
pros: 4000 SPM stroke gives a clean shear
cons: 20 inch blade is shorter than the 24 inch models

products.name: Greenworks 40V 24-Inch Cordless Hedge Trimmer, 1-Inch Capacity, Tool Only
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V is a tool-only 24-inch trimmer with a one-inch capacity and a three-sided wrap-around handle with a cushioned overmold grip. It is built for owners of the Greenworks 40V battery family.

The 40V platform has the voltage headroom to hold blade speed in thicker growth, and the long blade suits formal hedges. With no battery in the box, the cost to a new buyer is higher than the listing suggests.

Compared with the brushless 24-inch, you get a known platform and a bigger capacity but must supply your own power. Oil the blade after each use and store batteries indoors. Over several seasons the battery is the part that decides how long the tool stays useful, and platform packs are far easier to replace. It suits an owner who already has a Greenworks mower or blower and wants one pack to do everything.
products.bestFor: Greenworks 40V owners who want a long, capable trimmer.
pros: 24 inch blade with one inch capacity
cons: Battery and charger are not included
Heavy at the tip when fully extended

products.name: Ryobi 22-Inch 18-Volt Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The Ryobi 22-inch is a straightforward 18V trimmer built for the ONE+ battery platform, one of the broadest in home tools. The listing is sparse, so check whether a battery and charger are included.

Its value is the platform: spare batteries are easy to find, and the same packs run blowers, drills and mowers. A 22-inch blade is the sweet spot for coverage against tip weight.

Against the Greenworks, it lacks stated brushless design or capacity, so treat it as a dependable general-purpose tool. Oil the blade and store packs indoors. If you already own ONE+ batteries, the trimmer slots straight in and costs little to add. A common owner complaint with platform trimmers is buying the bare tool and forgetting the battery, so read the title twice.
products.bestFor: Ryobi ONE+ owners who want a balanced 22-inch blade.
pros: Joins the large ONE+ battery family
22 inch blade balances reach and weight

products.name: 24-Inch Cordless Hedge Trimmer, Two 2.0Ah Batteries, 180° Handle
products.description:
This is a 24-inch trimmer with MN65 steel dual-action blades, a low-noise 2,400 SPM motor and two 2.0Ah batteries that together claim up to 80 minutes of runtime. A rotating handle moves through 180 degrees, so you can cut tops and sides without twisting your wrist.

Compared with the brushless 24-inch, it has a brushed-class stroke rate and likely lower efficiency, but it is the cheapest long-blade kit here. The second battery keeps you working while the first charges.

Check spare battery availability and warranty, and oil the blade after each use. Because the battery pair is small, plan on a charge between jobs and avoid draining the cells to empty. Check the handle rotation lock before each job, as a loose lock makes the trimmer feel unstable at full reach.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a long blade with spare power.
cons: Lower stroke rate than the brushless picks

buyingCriteria.explanation: A brushless motor, as on the 24-inch kit and Greenworks 24V, saves energy, but only if the battery is big enough to feed it. Two batteries give you continuity on long hedges, while a single 2.0Ah pack stops after perhaps 30 minutes of real use. Brushless also tends to start under load more smoothly, which helps when the blade meets a thick stem. Owners who trim weekly in summer notice the difference first in battery life and motor heat. The practical test is whether you can finish your hedge on one pack; if not, buy the kit with two.

A 1200-watt label on a battery trimmer is peak input, not continuous cutting power. Compare cut capacity, stroke rate and the blade gap instead. Honest specs are inches and strokes per minute. A manufacturer who lists strokes per minute and capacity is giving you verifiable numbers. Honest specs also include how long the battery runs under load, which few listings state. Capacity claims are the more useful number, since blade gaps decide what is cut.

The Greenworks 24V runs 4000 SPM on 20 inches, while the budget 24-inch runs 2400 SPM. Fast strokes cut cleanly; long blades cover ground. Soft, regular hedges favor length; stiff stems favor speed. Cutting in sweeping arcs lets either design work at its best. A shorter blade at a higher stroke rate is also easier to control around corners and finials. For a tall hedge, the lighter and faster option usually tires you less over an afternoon.

The Greenworks 40V is sold without a battery. If you do not already own the pack, add its cost before comparing. The Ryobi listing leaves the question open, so check it. Shared batteries across a mower, blower and trimmer cut the real cost of ownership. Compare the cost of a spare pack against the cost of the whole kit before deciding. A new platform makes sense only if you plan to buy more tools for it.

A 24-inch blade extended in front of you is far harder to hold than a 20-inch one. A rotating handle or a wrap-around grip reduces wrist strain. Plan breaks every fifteen minutes. A harness or strap is a cheap upgrade for any 24-inch trimmer. Consider the height of the hedge too, since shoulder-high tops are where a long blade hurts most.

MN65 and hardened steel blades hold an edge but still dull on thorny wood or wire. Check the blade for nicks each season and have it sharpened. A blade sharpened once a season cuts much cleaner than a dull one. Stones, wire and nails in old hedges are the usual cause of chipped teeth. A quick pass of a sharpening stone along the edge can restore a lot of lost cutting performance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor type
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored brushless motors, listed on the 24-inch kit and the Greenworks 24V. Brushless designs were credited for lower wear. We cross-read every motor claim against the blade and battery specs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cutting capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated capacity, with the 1.1 inch Greenworks 24V highest. Capacity was cross-checked against blade type. A fast stroke earned credit for cut quality but not for capacity. Listings that gave only a wattage figure scored lower on transparency.

howWeEvaluated.title: Kit contents
howWeEvaluated.description: We credited two-battery bundles and noted the tool-only Greenworks 40V. Kit contents decided how many points a tool-only listing lost. We gave bundles with spare packs extra credit for runtime.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed blade length, handles and tip weight. Handles and balance were judged from the listing photos and descriptions.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated patterns on short runtime, heavy tips and spare battery availability. Owner reports of fading packs in the second year shaped the battery advice. We checked how consistent spare-pack availability appeared to be.

cards.label: Long blade
cards.text: The 24-inch kits cover a long hedge in fewer passes but weigh more at the tip.

cards.label: Fast stroke
cards.text: The Greenworks 24V at 4000 SPM makes cleaner cuts on stiff stems with a shorter blade.

howToChoose.note: Pick length for soft, long hedges and speed for woody ones.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High stroke rate, capacity above an inch and a brushless motor.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 24V and the Greenworks 40V are the best fits.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a long hedge, trim several times a year and want brushless and a spare pack.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a short hedge, where a basic cordless kit does fine.

maintenance.why: Resin builds up and stalls the motor. Run a dry cloth over the blade after each use. Sharpen or replace the blades every few seasons because a dull edge tears stems and drains the battery faster.
Loose bolts cause uneven cutting. Use a snug driver and recheck after the first hour.
Temperature extremes degrade lithium cells. Do not leave batteries in a hot car.
Clippings block cooling air. Blow out the vents with a soft brush.
Grease seepage signals a worn seal. Wear gloves while checking the gearbox. Wipe off any seepage and note whether it returns.

faq.q: Is brushless worth the extra cost?
faq.a: For frequent use on long hedges, yes. It runs cooler and wears less. It also gives you a quieter tool, which is a bonus in tight neighborhoods. Quiet operation is another advantage in dense neighborhoods.

They are peak input figures. Compare capacity and stroke rate instead. Treat the label as an ad claim rather than a spec. A spare pack on a long hedge is worth more than a longer blade, so buy the same capacity for predictable runtime.

faq.q: How long does one battery last?
faq.a: Often 30 to 40 minutes of real cutting. Two batteries double it. Battery temperature and blade sharpness change this by a large margin. Cold batteries also deliver less, so warm the pack in your pocket on a chilly morning.
